name: Adbhuta Narayana Temple, Thrikkodithanam
deity: Vishnu as Adbhuta Narayana, 'the wondrous Narayana', standing in four-armed form
period: A Divya Desam of Malai Nadu, sung by Nammalvar in the Nalayira Divya Prabandham
summary: Near Changanassery, Vishnu is worshipped as Adbhuta Narayana at Thrikkodithanam — a Malai Nadu Divya Desam sung by Nammalvar, held by tradition to have been consecrated by Sahadeva, youngest of the Pandavas.

sections.history: Thrikkodithanam — Thirukkadithanam in the hymns — is one of the 108 Divya Desams, the abodes of Vishnu sung by the Alvars in the Nalayira Divya Prabandham, and a shrine of Malai Nadu praised by Nammalvar. It stands in the green country just east of Changanassery in Kottayam district. Its origins are placed by tradition in the age of the Chera Perumals. It is also one of five temples of the region that tradition links with the Pandava brothers.
sections.architecture: The temple follows the Kerala manner: a sanctum (srikovil) beneath sloping roofs, enclosed by the nalambalam cloister, within a walled compound entered past the balikkal altar stone and the flagstaff. The four-armed image of Vishnu stands in the sanctum. The compound keeps the restrained timber-and-stone architecture shared by the other Pandava shrines of the region.
sections.legends: Tradition holds that after the Mahabharata war the five Pandavas came to this country and each consecrated a shrine of Vishnu: Yudhishthira at Thrichittatt, Bhima at Puliyur, Arjuna at Aranmula, Nakula at Thiruvanvandoor — and Sahadeva, the youngest, here at Thrikkodithanam. The lord he enshrined is worshipped as Adbhuta Narayana, 'the wondrous Narayana'. Pilgrims sometimes honour the five brothers by visiting all five temples together as a single circuit.
sections.festivals: The annual festival is celebrated with flag hoisting and processions, and the festival of lamps on Karthika in the month of Vrischikam (November–December) fills the temple with flame. Vaikunta Ekadashi is also observed with special worship, and devotees making the circuit of the five Pandava temples often include Thrikkodithanam.
sections.experience: Thrikkodithanam is a village temple of deep calm, close enough to Changanassery for an easy visit yet far from the town's noise. Come at dusk to see the lamps lit along the compound, and consider joining the circuit of the Pandava shrines that continues south around Chengannur and Aranmula.

visit.timings: Open daily with morning and evening darshan and a midday closure, following the temple's own schedule; festival days are crowded. Confirm current timings locally before you visit.
visit.dressCode: Traditional dress is expected: by Kerala temple custom men usually enter bare-chested in a mundu or dhoti, and women in saree or other traditional dress; footwear is left outside. Follow posted rules and the guidance of temple staff.
visit.photography: Photography is not permitted in and around the sanctum; follow posted rules and the guidance of temple staff.
visit.gettingThere: Thrikkodithanam is a short drive east of Changanassery in Kottayam district. Changanassery has a railway station on the Ernakulam–Kottayam–Kollam line, Kottayam is nearby, and Kochi has the nearest airport.
